bounds.synchronization: Use explicit deferred gates and event ordering, not sleep-derived success. Watchdog failures are failures, not passes. No unbounded stress loops.

cases.purpose: Standalone registration, hostile shadow and literal dispatch
cases.setup: Use public root Shell and exactly the packed alias plugin, without registering grep. Repeat in a fresh Shell with a grep definition that increments a counter then throws. Direct contexts also supply an invoke hook that counts and throws.
expected: Both aliases work with no registered grep
Shadow grep and context.invoke counters remain zero
Literal fgrep prints $(touch sentinel) followed by newline and creates no sentinel
Registration adds egrep and fgrep, not grep; existing registry entries are unchanged
A collision on the second alias cannot partially register the first; explicit replace affects only the two aliases

cases.purpose: Owned fragments for reused Buffer input across chunks and EOF
cases.setup: For each alias, yield the same Buffer repeatedly; overwrite it only when the producer is advanced, and overwrite again in finally. Run whole 8-byte records, then four-byte split fragments. Also use this source as a VFS readFile result. Do not mutate concurrently during an outstanding awaited transient write.
expected: Status zero; exact owned output bytes match the fixture; stderr is empty
Direct byte sink, internal pipe-to-file bytes and terminal buffered bytes are recorded separately
A shared runtime-owned-output defect is reported to root without editing shared code
cases.provenance: AGENTS producer-reuse ownership contract; independently chosen bytes

cases.purpose: Cumulative shell budgets without resetting at alias boundaries
cases.setup: Prepare an 8192-byte input by repeating keep:01 newline 1024 times. Each of two sequential alias invocations selects exactly 4096 bytes using max-count 512; use a single enclosing Shell execution with a 6144-byte output budget through its documented public limit API after handoff. Repeat nested invocation and a pipeline where applicable; do not conflate output accounting with regex queue budgets.
expected: Individually permitted output does not create a fresh shared shell budget for the second alias
No successful unbounded 8192-byte collected result
Preserve selected budget failure and drain invocation-owned cleanup before public settlement
If the public API cannot express this budget, record unavailable with exact evidence rather than inventing a setting
cases.provenance: Shared command contract; family limits are not one shared shell budget

cases.purpose: Family worker concurrency, queue bounds and sibling ownership
cases.setup: Reuse one createGrepAliasCommands family in two public Shell registries, with maxWorkers 1, maxQueuedRequests 1 and maxQueuedBytes 4096. At most three invocations, mixed egrep and fgrep, with held input/output gates. Observe worker lifecycle through a supported external Node mechanism, not private module exports. Use a third bounded request to exercise queue admission. Separately created standalone factories are a control with distinct executors, not a violation.
expected: Aliases from one family share the configured executor limit
Queue overflow has an observable bounded error and is not silently accepted
Cancellation/cleanup of one invocation does not cancel a sibling or another Shell's lease
Record lifecycle events and output bytes; inability to force queued work is unmeasured, not a pass
cases.provenance: Provided family-sharing proposal and RegexExecutionOptions contract

cases.purpose: Cancellation before work and during cooperative acquisition
cases.setup: Use each alias with a pre-aborted signal, then abort while an owned file read or worker request is pending. Use an object reason and an errno-shaped object reason. Keep gates bounded and release them in teardown.
expected: Pre-aborted execution causes no VFS reads, stdin advance or worker admission
Caller reason identity wins at public settlement
Supplied signal reaches VFS operations
Public settlement waits for registered cooperative cleanup, not arbitrary uncooperative reads
No new owned acquisition after cleanup closes admission
cases.provenance: Shared cooperative invocation cleanup and signal contracts

cases.purpose: Synchronous cleanup registration before any acquisition
cases.setup: Direct command contexts record registerCleanup, first stdin next, VFS reads and observable worker creation. A registration hook first throws a sentinel before acquisition; a second hook calls the supplied cleanup synchronously. Then capture cleanup and invoke it concurrently with finally and repeated cleanup calls.
expected: Registration precedes input, file and worker acquisition
Throwing registration prevents acquisition and preserves the selected error
Cleanup requested during registration prevents later admission
Overlapping cleanup shares completion and does not retire resources twice
A context without registerCleanup still performs finally cleanup
cases.provenance: Shared cooperative invocation cleanup contract; no author implementation assumed

cases.purpose: Iterator return failure and cooperative cleanup failure precedence
cases.setup: Quiet matching causes early source closure. The source return method either throws synchronously or rejects asynchronously with a sentinel. Separately register a cooperative cleanup that rejects, and combine it with an exact caller-abort reason. Repeat both aliases without endlessly pending work.
expected: Return is attempted on early closure and not called twice by one iterator owner
An otherwise successful operation cannot silently hide the return failure; retain exact raw rejection or explicit nonzero diagnostic outcome for contract classification
A registered cleanup-only failure rejects public exec unchanged; nonzero command status does not hide it
Caller abort still wins by reason identity; all secondary failures are observed
cases.provenance: Shared ByteSource readBytes contract and public cleanup precedence

cases.setup: For both aliases, supply two selected lines in separate chunks, and a sink whose first write is held by a deferred gate. Copy bytes inside the sink before resolving. Repeat with rejection of that gate and a stderr sink that rejects during an invalid-expression diagnostic.
expected: At most one sink write is in flight; command cannot report completion while its awaited write is held
No second output write before the first settles
Sink rejection is not success and does not orphan cooperative cleanup
Do not assert zero speculative input reads beyond a public guarantee
cases.provenance: Awaited ByteSink writes and bounded streaming contract

cases.setup: Hold stdin next, a VFS read, and a sink write in separate bounded subcases. Abort with an exact sentinel, then explicitly reject the held operation. Record unhandledRejection/rejectionHandled events in an isolated verifier process and remove listeners in finally.
expected: The caller reason remains the public outcome
Every late host rejection is observed
No late output publication or new owned work after closed admission
Do not require public exec to wait for an opaque host promise before it is explicitly released

cases.purpose: Complex Shell pipelines, redirects and byte readback
scripts:
printf 'aa:1
bb:2
aa:3
' | egrep '^aa:' | fgrep -v ':9' > selected.txt; fgrep 'aa:' selected.txt

set -o pipefail; printf 'aa:1
bb:2
aa:3
' | egrep '^aa:' | fgrep absent
expected: First script status zero, selected.txt exact pipeline-expected fixture, stdout same bytes, empty stderr
Second script status one with empty stdout and stderr
Register only documented public command providers needed by these scripts; malicious grep remains unused
No public alias subpath assumption
cases.provenance: Independent shell algebra and hand-chosen fixture bytes

cases.purpose: Early pipeline close with owned cleanup and concurrent sibling
cases.setup: A VFS stream supplies at most 65536 bytes of keep:01 newline records; head selects one line. Run a sibling alias invocation in the same family and dispose the first Shell concurrently with its completion. Use recorded cooperative lifecycle gates.
expected: Successful pipeline stdout is exactly keep:01 newline
Internal downstream close is not misreported as caller abort
exec and repeated/concurrent dispose await registered cleanup owed by that Shell
Sibling-owned worker use remains valid
No global worker-zero requirement while sibling still owns work
cases.provenance: Shared internal-pipe and cooperative cleanup contract

cases.purpose: Substitution, grouped pipelines and alias error attribution
expected: First script status zero, stdout count-expected fixture and empty stderr
Second script status zero, stdout aa:3 newline and empty stderr
Direct invalid-option/missing-file diagnostics name the invoked alias, not shadow grep
Nested execution retains shared signal and budgets; no shell-string dispatch inside the alias
